## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

T636 (two fascicles, alt. title 無極寶經) is [竺法護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E6%B3%95%E8%AD%B7)'s Western Jin translation of a Mahāyāna *samādhi*-sūtra extolling the *wújíbǎo sānmèi* — the "Boundless-Treasure Samādhi" — as a meditative concentration in which the bodhisattva acquires inexhaustible spiritual wealth. The text is the underlying Indic source for the Eastern Jin parallel [T637](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0274) (*Bǎorúlái sānmèi jīng*) by [Gītamitra](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%A5%87%E5%A4%9A%E8%9C%9C).

**Abstract**

T636 is unanimously ascribed to [竺法護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E6%B3%95%E8%AD%B7) in the canonical bibliographies; the *[Chū sānzàng jì jí](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6s/KR6s0084)* (T2145) lists it among his works. Date bracket follows Dharmarakṣa's productive period (266–308). The text develops the metaphor of the *bǎo* (treasure / wish-fulfilling jewel) as a figure for the *prajñāpāramitā*-mind: just as a jewel reflects all colours without itself having colour, so the bodhisattva's mind in *samādhi* reflects all *dharma*s without grasping. The text is closely paralleled by [T637](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0274) but is more concise; both are independent Chinese versions of the same Indic source. Boucher (2008) discusses Dharmarakṣa's stylistic profile in such *samādhi*-sūtras.
